contents.entry: Pointers: parent, siblings, schema, shared volumes
Mechanism: reading coq/gate on the head sha
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
Retries: three attempts, then recover and report
Many agents at once: the collision answer
State paths written and the cleanup script for each

pointers.shared: Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

purpose.sentence: For every open pull request head in a forge snapshot, the Go service turns the GitHub commit status coq/gate into one gate.verdict record, green, red or pending, that every later node reads and no agent can edit.
purpose.is: The verdict the agent can read and cannot change (D05, T04, I03 F8a): the status lives on the commit on GitHub, is posted only by the Jenkins controller (N-25), and is a required status check on main, so GitHub itself refuses a merge without it.
Deterministic and idempotent: the same snapshot yields the same verdict; a verdict is written once per pull request, head sha and state, so a poll every tick writes nothing while nothing changes.
purpose.is-not: Not a test runner and not a status poster: N-23, N-24 and N-25 run the pods and post coq/gate; this node only reads.
Not a tester seat: the tester role is retired (D11, card C39; WO-20261013-3eac in L07 section 5 item 4).
purpose.decisions: D05 (C43, GitHub required status check coq/gate), D06 (C44, poll every tick), D11 (C39), V05 (infrastructure retried, assertions never), T04 (a verdict the agent cannot edit).

record.field: When N-04 polled and its counter that only grows; one snapshot per poll tick (tick:poll, forge.poll_seconds 30, N-06).
The sha of main at poll time and the coq/gate status on it (N-10 and N-26 use main_gate; this node copies main_sha into each verdict for the Machine screen).

One entry per open pull request (N-04 pr): number, ticket (from the title, WO-YYYYMMDD-xxxx), head_sha, head_ref, base_ref, mergeable (MERGEABLE, CONFLICTING, UNKNOWN), draft, labels, gate (the coq/gate status: state success, failure, error, pending, or absent; description; target_url; updated_at), gate_page (the coq/gate-page status when posted), statuses_deferred (true when N-04 could not read this head's statuses in this poll, so a missing status is not read as absent; mechanism step 2).
N-04 marks a snapshot stale when a poll failed and the previous one was re-published; this node skips a stale snapshot (nothing changed).
record.join: The newest review.passed or review.changes record per head is read from the store by this node, not carried in the snapshot.
Whether the head is from a fork is read from head_ref's repository owner in the pr entry (N-04 pr.head_ref); a fork is a different owner.

input.starts-when: A forge.snapshot record is committed. The node is level-triggered: it reads the whole snapshot every time and compares with the newest gate.verdict per pull request and head.

record.field: pr number, colon, head_sha, colon, verdict; a second write with the same key is refused by N-01 with 409 and read as already written.
The work order id from the title; a title with no ticket yields verdict red with reason no-ticket (merge.sh held outcome: its title names no ticket).
The head the status is on.

green (code 201, status success), red (code 422, status failure), pending (code 100, status pending, or absent within the absent bound), missing (code 500, status absent past the absent bound or error past three re-runs), superseded (code 100, status error with description superseded, the older head of a newer push; ci/README.md abortPrevious).
The target_url of the status (the Jenkins run) and the gate page url; the fix attempt's brief links them.
GitHub's updated_at on the status, so staleness is a fact not a guess.

output.ends-when: Every pull request in the snapshot has a gate.verdict for its current head and current state. Green re-enters N-02 as a reviewer-phase claim (dag.md section 4); red and missing enter N-11 as failure records; pending ends the traversal and the next snapshot starts a new one.

mechanism.where: Go package gate inside the service; a pure function Verdicts(snapshot, previous verdicts, now, config) returns the verdict intents, and the engine writes them.
mechanism.step: Read the newest gate.verdict per (pr, head_sha) from N-01 in one read transaction, and the forge.snapshot that started this traversal.

A pull request whose statuses_deferred is true is skipped this traversal, and a stale snapshot is skipped whole: a status GitHub did not answer is unknown, never absent (doc 31 rule: a deadline failure does not prove anything; L14 section 4.6). The skip is counted, never recorded, because the next snapshot retries.

Map each pull request's gate state to a verdict: success to green 201; failure to red 422; pending to pending 100; error with description superseded to superseded 100; error otherwise to pending 100 on the first two sightings and missing 500 on the third sighting of error on the same head (the infrastructure ladder of N-24 and N-25 already retried; a third error is a pods or Jenkins fault for the system lane); absent to pending 100 while now minus the pull request's head pushed_at is below gate.absent_seconds (default 1800; the Jenkins full run budget 30 minutes, Jenkinsfile line 24 cited in L07 section 5 item 8), else missing 500.

A head older than the pull request's current head gets no new verdict; its last verdict stands and N-09 never reads it because N-09 matches on the current head (gate.sh heads_match, lifted). The older head's open reviewer run, if any, is ended by N-12 through the dispatch deadline, not by this node.
Compare each intent with the newest stored verdict for the same (pr, head_sha); write only on a change of verdict. The idempotency key makes a concurrent duplicate a 409 (many-agents).

A draft pull request yields pending with reason draft and is never green; a fork pull request yields red with reason fork (the Jenkins fork guard runs nothing for a fork, L07 section 4; a fork never merges by machine).
Write the verdicts; a green verdict is also the record N-02 reads to grant the reviewer-phase lease (re-entry), so nothing else needs to wake anything.
mechanism.invariant: No agent and no seat can write a gate.verdict: N-01 refuses the kind from any writer but the service, and the status on GitHub is posted only by the Jenkins controller's token which no pod and no seat holds (L07 section 4: the GitHub token never enters a pod).
A verdict never changes for a (pr, head, state) triple; a new state is a new record, so the history of a head is append-only and readable on the Machine screen.
mechanism.diagram: flowchart LR S["forge.snapshot"] --> E{"statuses_deferred for this PR, or stale snapshot?"} E -- yes --> K["skip, next snapshot retries"] E -- no --> M{"coq/gate state"} M -- success --> G["green 201"] M -- failure --> R["red 422"] M -- pending --> P["pending 100"] M -- "error superseded" --> U["superseded 100"] M -- "error x3" --> X["missing 500"] M -- "absent past bound" --> X M -- "absent in bound" --> P G --> D{"changed since last verdict?"} R --> D P --> D U --> D X --> D D -- no --> K D -- yes --> W["write gate.verdict (idempotency key pr:head:verdict)"] W --> N02["green: N-02 reviewer claim"] W --> N11["red or missing: N-11"]

start.sentence: Nothing here starts by an agent typing.
start.by: N-06 broadcasts the tick:poll entity every forge.poll_seconds (default 30; Symphony polling.interval_ms 30000, I03 section 6); N-04 polls GitHub and writes forge.snapshot; the committed snapshot starts this node. Webhooks, when added, are accelerators that make N-04 poll sooner (its forge_poll_now record) and change nothing here (D06).
start.restart: After a crash the next snapshot re-derives every verdict from GitHub and the stored verdicts; no memory is needed.

wait.fallback: skip this traversal; the next snapshot retries; three skips in a row write store.unreachable 500 once (same latch as N-07)
retry 1 s, 2 s, 4 s; then the verdict is derived again from the next snapshot, so nothing is lost

wait.on: coq/gate appearing on a new head
wait.fallback: missing 500 to N-11, which re-posts pr.opened through a gate dispatch (N-07 step 8) up to three times, then dead and one card

wait.timeout: gate.pending_seconds, default 3600 (the Jenkins budget plus the ladder's 300 s rung)
wait.fallback: missing 500 with reason pending-timeout; same path as absent

waits.rule: This node holds no GitHub call; every GitHub wait is N-04's, with its own timeout and the statuses_deferred and stale fields.

step.name: verdict write
step.then: derived again on the next snapshot; a gate.write.failed 500 is written once per head when the third write fails

step.name: missing gate
step.backoff: N-11 backoff min(10 s x 2^(n-1), 300 s)
step.then: dead record by N-11, one card by N-28 naming the head and the last Jenkins url

retries.not-retried: A red verdict is never retried by this node: a failing assertion is the worker's fix (V05); the fix is attempt n plus 1 of the worker phase through N-11.
retries.report: Every then clause is a 500 record; N-28 builds exactly one card per latched kind and head.

many-agents.readers: Any number of seats read gate.verdict records; a reviewer brief (N-19) cites the verdict id and the gate url; nobody reads GitHub statuses directly from a seat (permissions).
many-agents.two-writers: Two service processes during a restart overlap may both derive the same verdict from the same snapshot; the idempotency key pr:head:verdict makes the second write a 409 that is logged and counted, never a second record.
many-agents.two-snapshots: Two snapshots in flight (a slow write and a fast next poll) can write the same verdict in either order; the key makes them one. A state that flips pending, green, pending between snapshots yields two records with different keys, which is the true history.
many-agents.seat-cannot-edit: A seat that tries to post a gate.verdict or a commit status is refused: N-01 by writer identity, GitHub by token; the deny list of the seat layer (N-13) also denies gh api on statuses. The reviewer reads a number it cannot change (T04).
many-agents.stale-head: A seat working an older head posts its result with the old head sha; N-09 matches on the current head and ignores it; no lock is needed because heads are facts in the snapshot.
many-agents.test: Test case two-snapshots-one-verdict: two Verdicts calls over the same snapshot write one record and one 409 (checklist c-idempotent).

emits.acts: N-02 grants the reviewer-phase lease; N-09 reads it with review.passed
N-11 schedules the worker fix attempt with the gate url
nobody; the Machine screen shows it

state-paths.root: $COQ_STATE as in ../N-07/spec.xml#state-paths; path elements in N-45's generator form.
state-paths.path: Rows of kind gate.verdict; verdicts of merged tickets older than retention are pruned after the verified record (N-01's row).
One line per pull request per traversal with the mapped state; rotated daily.
state-paths.never: No file under the repository; no copy of a GitHub status anywhere but the store.

out.note: drawn in dag.md as N-08 to RE and N-09; red and missing are failure records of N-11's input shape

re-entry.as: reviewer-phase claim on the same ticket

upstream-of-input.note: the status this node reads; N-25 to N-04 is the drawn edge

schema.defs: gate_verdict; forge_snapshot is a reference to ../N-04/record.schema.json#/$defs/forge_snapshot; base as in N-07.

permissions.reads: forge.snapshot and gate.verdict records in N-01.
permissions.writes: gate.verdict, gate.write.failed, store.unreachable records; the gate log.
permissions.never: No GitHub call from this node (N-04 owns the token and the poll); no edit of any status; no pane; no prompt.
permissions.seat: Seats read verdicts through their brief and the store's read socket; a seat's settings deny gh api on commit statuses and deny any write of kind gate.verdict (N-13 renders the deny list).

counter.name: gate_pending
counter.from: open heads with newest verdict pending

counter.name: gate_missing_open
counter.from: open heads with newest verdict missing

gauge.name: gate_pending_age_seconds
gauge.from: now minus the newest pending verdict's at, per head

lamp.name: gate
lamp.green: every open head has a verdict newer than two poll intervals
lamp.red: a head without a verdict for three poll intervals, or missing open

alert.to: N-41 and, after N-11's third attempt, one card by N-28

runbook.bring-up: N-25 must post coq/gate and main protection must require it (N-25 runbook); then set gate.enabled true; proof: a gate.verdict record for the newest open pull request.
runbook.read-status: Scheduler.Status lists open heads with their newest verdict; the Machine screen shows one pull request with its verdict history.
runbook.recover-missing: Nothing by hand: missing goes to N-11, which re-posts pr.opened through a gate dispatch; after three the card names the Jenkins url and the owner decides. A hand re-run in Jenkins is a break glass through N-42, recorded.
runbook.registry: Generated into shared/cleanup-registry.json from the state-paths element (../N-45/spec.xml#state-paths).
